topics.label: Introduction and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture within the cancer course and sets out its learning objectives.

topics.label: Mutation accumulation and susceptibility to cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations can produce cancer through clonal evolution and why their consequences depend on the cells and conditions in which they arise.

topics.label: Environmental contributions to cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the evidence and uncertainty surrounding how environmental exposures contribute to cancer rather than cancer being simply inevitable or random.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections can drive cancer, using Burkitt lymphoma to develop the interaction between infection and malignant transformation.

topics.label: Environmental carcinogens and mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental carcinogens produce DNA damage, showing how their mutagenic effects depend on their interactions with cellular processes.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish initiating mutations from the promotional conditions that allow mutated cells to proliferate into tumours.

topics.label: Developmental and tissue-specific susceptibility to carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how susceptibility depends on the exposed tissue's biological state and conclude by placing that specificity within the preceding account of carcinogenic mechanisms.

topics.label: Methods for identifying and assessing carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how carcinogenic effects can be inferred or tested and why the resulting evidence requires careful interpretation.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This closing synthesises the lecture's conclusions about environmental cancer risks and their assessment into a final reflection on risk–benefit decisions.
